speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any headaches, vision changes, or seizures alongside these neurological symptoms? I also need to know if you have any history of cancer or recent infections.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of cancer, particularly breast or lung cancer, or any recent weight loss? I suspect a possible brain metastasis or primary tumor given the combination of focal neurological deficits and rapid cognitive decline.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known history of HIV, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Noncompliance with medications for over 2 years. Social history: Information not provided

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of untreated HIV, I am concerned about opportunistic infections or primary CNS lymphoma. REQUEST TEST: Brain MRI with contrast and CSF analysis for JC virus and toxoplasmosis.
